transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Alex Ramirez (CTO, Silverwood), Priya Singh (ML Engineer), Jordan Lee (Product Manager)
Links shared: https://docs.redwood.ai/hosted-api, https://app.redwood.ai/console (demo account), pricing sheet (sent post-call)

-- Transcript (auto) --
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE working with you all, and with me is Ethan our solutions engineer. Quick check, everyone's audio OK?
[00:08] Alex: Yep, all good here, Alex from Silverwood. Thanks for doing this demo today.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, Priya here. We're particularly interested in streaming and how retries work under load.
[00:18] Ethan: Great, that's exactly what we'll focus on — streaming, generation params, and retry patterns. I'll share my screen in a sec and demo the Console + a simple cURL/SDK flow.
[00:31] Ethan: (shares screen) OK, this is the Hosted API demo environment, we have a sample chat session. First thing, streaming — you can request chunked responses so the client gets tokens as they're generated. That's the same API surface whether you're on Hosted or Dedicated.
[00:45] Maya: Quick note — streaming helps lower perceived latency for users since you can render partial responses early. It doesn't change total token compute but improves UX.
[00:58] Jordan: Does streaming increase rate-limit usage or cost?
[01:02] Ethan: It doesn't change per-token billing. The request itself is the same; streaming just changes how the response is delivered. There is slightly more egress for many small packets, but it's negligible compared to token cost.
[01:17] Alex: Got it. For our use case, we want a 95th percentile under 300ms for short prompts — is that realistic with Hosted?
[01:23] Maya: For short prompts it's possible; it depends on model choice and region. We publish perf profiles for verified models. If you need strict SLOs, Dedicated gives stronger predictability, but many customers hit sub-300ms with Hosted by using lower-latency model variants and prefix caching.
[01:41] Priya: You mentioned prefix/KV cache — can you explain?
[01:44] Ethan: Sure, prefix caching caches past key-value state for repeated system prompts or shared context. If your prompts share a lot of the same prefix, cost and latency drop because we can reuse KV cache instead of recomputing.
[01:58] Ethan: Now, generation params — temperature, top_p, max_tokens, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, stop sequences. We'll demo how each affects output and determinism.
[02:10] (demo: cURL example on screen)
[02:18] Ethan: Example request: 
POST /v1/generate 
{ "model":"rw-1-small", "messages": [...], "temperature":0.2, "max_tokens":150, "stream":true }
[02:34] Priya: We use a safety filter and a post-processing step, any recommended values to reduce hallucinations?
[02:40] Ethan: Lower temperature helps, also using system-level instructions and retrieval augmentation reduces hallucinations. Use a beam of safety checks in your pipeline; Redwood also supports structured output and function-calling to force outputs into schema.
[02:55] Alex: About retries — if we see transient 500s during high throughput, what's the recommended client-side strategy?
[03:00] Ethan: Recommended pattern is idempotency keys for requests where appropriate, and exponential backoff with jitter: start 200-500ms, double, cap around 8-10s. For streaming requests, you should treat them as non-idempotent unless you can reconstitute the last-token state or use a session-based approach.
[03:20] Maya: I'll add that Redwood's SDKs include retry helpers and you'll get a header with request_id to correlate server logs for triage.
[03:31] Jordan: Do you provide SDKs in Node/Python?
[03:34] Ethan: Yes, official SDKs for Node and Python, examples for Go and Java in the repo. We also have a lightweight cURL example which is nice for quick tests.
[03:45] Priya: For benchmarking, what metrics should we collect?
[03:48] Ethan: Tokens/sec, latency p50/p95/p99, success/error rates, and memory/CPU on client side if you're batching. Also collect request size (prompt length) since that impacts compute. We'll share a benchmark script.
[04:05] (demo: streaming response shows partial tokens rendering)
[04:28] Alex: Can you show retries in action? Like a simulated transient error?
[04:31] Ethan: Sure, I can simulate a 503 in the test endpoint — watch the SDK's retry with exponential backoff and how the request_id is logged.
[04:48] (demo: simulated 503, SDK retries, eventual success)
[05:10] Priya: Nice. On rate limits: if we burst above our quota, is there graceful degradation?
[05:15] Maya: Yes, we expose quota headers and a 429 with Retry-After. You can route to a fallback model variant or degrade to cached answers. For high-criticality flows, Dedicated with burst capacity and autoscaling is an option.
[05:32] Alex: Security — can you recap the hosted data retention policy and encryption?
[05:36] Maya: Hosted: by default we retain logs for X days (we customize by contract), all data at rest encrypted with customer-managed KMS on Private/Dedicated. We support SOC 2, and can provide network diagrams and the security pack. We'll share SOC2/ISO docs after the call.
[05:53] Jordan: Any options for VPC peering for hosted?
[05:56] Ethan: Hosted doesn't do full VPC peering; for that we recommend Redwood Private. Hosted supports encryption in transit and tenant isolation, and we have contract terms for data residency.
[06:08] Priya: If we want to test with our prompt set and 1k qps for a week, what does that look like operationally?
[06:14] Ethan: We usually run a benchmark with a test API key, collect metrics, and then propose either Hosted with a reserved burst or Dedicated capacity depending on sustained qps and SLOs. We'll size GPU units and recommend batching/quantization profiles.
[06:26] Maya: Actionable next steps — we'll send pricing, security docs, and a benchmark kit. Ethan will help run the initial test.
[06:36] Alex: Sounds good. One last thing — cost forecasting: is there a tool for simulating monthly costs given traffic?
[06:41] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console has a cost estimator where you input qps, average prompt length, and it estimates tokens and monthly spend. We'll share a live demo link.
[06:52] (customer questions wrap up)
[07:00] Maya: Quick recap: 1) we'll send pricing + SOC2 + network diagram, 2) Ethan will share benchmark script + test dataset, 3) Priya will send expected traffic profile, 4) schedule benchmark run week of 12/20.
[07:18] Alex: Thanks all, appreciate the thorough demo.
[07:22] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[07:25] Maya: Thanks everyone, bye.
